handbook: Code of Practice on Sewerage and Sanitary Works
section: Annex A - Requirements for Construction of RC Trench
sourceFile: Capability Testing Pack/Annex A - The rules/SSW Annex A (b).docx
description: Table 11 - RC Trench Width. Minimum internal width of the trench depends on sewer depth and pipe nominal diameter.

interpretation.targetElement: RC Trench specifically -- see elementType gate in src/rules/types.ts (requireElementType), same as Annex A(a)/(c)

table.note: Source table cell was blank/merged ('See Figure 2'). ASSUMPTION: inherits the 900+T formula from the row above, regardless of diameter. No sample scenario at depth > 3m uses diameter <= 300mm, so this is UNTESTED against ground truth.

openAmbiguities: The rule card gives two different definitions of T in two places: the main table says 'T = 2 x haunching + diameter', but one 'Rule Scenario' requirement block says 'T = 900mm + (2 x Thickness of haunching) + nominal sewer diameter' (an extra '900mm +' folded into T's own definition). VERIFIED BY CALCULATION (not assumed): plugging Scenario 02-compliant's numbers (diameter 350mm, haunching 125mm, expected width 1500mm) into each definition -- the simple definition gives 900 + (2*125+350) = 1500mm, matching exactly; the definition with the extra 900 gives 900 + (900+2*125+350) = 2400mm, which does not match. The simple definition (main table) is the one used; the scenario text's extra '900mm +' is treated as a drafting/copy-paste error.

Scenarios 02-non-compliant and 03-non-compliant ('haunching not provided; width 1250mm') do not fail on arithmetic -- 900 + 2*0 + 350 = 1250mm, i.e. the built width exactly equals the zero-haunching minimum. They are still marked NON-COMPLIANT. Interpretation: once diameter > 300mm, the Code requires haunching thickness to be specified as part of the design -- its absence is a design/documentation failure, not a missing-data situation for us to flag as NEEDS_REVIEW. This is a deliberate departure from every other rule in this project (where missing data defaults to NEEDS_REVIEW): the distinction is between 'we failed to read a value that's on the drawing' (our extraction failure -> NEEDS_REVIEW) versus 'the drawing itself never specifies a value the Code requires it to specify' (a design failure -> NON_COMPLIANT). Diameter <= 300mm never needs haunching at all (flat 750mm rule), so this only applies once diameter > 300mm.
